items.text: In the Indian state of Gujarat, at least 141 people died and many were missing after a pedestrian bridge suddenly collapsed into the Machchu River. The incident happened only a week after the bridge had reopened. According to officials, the bridge was dangerously overcrowded at the time of the collapse because people were celebrating the Diwali festival. Some survivors clambered up the bridge’s broken netting, and others managed to swim to the river banks. Rescuers searched the murky waters, and divers scoured the riverbed for missing people. Local police questioned eight people about the collapse. The 230-meter structure was a popular tourist attraction known locally as Julto Pul. People built the swinging bridge in the 19th century during British rule. It was a swinging bridge. Difficult words: clamber (to climb with difficulty), murky (dark and dirty), scour (to search carefully). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A pedestrian bridge collapsed in India’s state of Gujarat. The bridge had reopened only a week earlier. Officials said that too many people were on the bridge when it collapsed . They were celebrating the Diwali festival. The bridge collapsed in the river, 141 people died, and many went missing. The incident happened at night, so it was difficult to search for them. Rescuers continued the next morning, and divers searched the dark waters of the river. The bridge was 230 meters high, and it was very popular with tourists. Local people called it a swinging bridge. Workers built it in the 19 th century when India was still under the rule of Great Britain. Difficult words: pedestrian bridge (a bridge which people walk on), collapse (to suddenly fall down), swing (to move from side to side). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A bridge collapses in India. It is a pedestrian bridge. A pedestrian bridge is for people to walk. This bridge is above a river. People celebrate the Diwali festival. Too many people are on the bridge. The bridge starts to move from side to side. Suddenly, it falls. 141 people die. Many people go missing . Some people swim to the river banks. Rescuers search the waters. It is not easy. The river is dark and dirty. Police investigate the event. They speak to eight people. In the 19th century, workers build the bridge. It is a popular place for tourists. People like the bridge. It moves when they walk on it. Difficult words: collapse (to suddenly fall down), go missing (when someone cannot be found), investigate (to find out what happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Seoul, South Korea, a Halloween stampede killed at least 153 people in a crowded nightlife area. The Halloween event was the first in three years that was free of coronavirus restrictions and social distancing. Many of the party goers wore masks and Halloween costumes. A huge crowd surged into an alley, and some witnesses described the crowd became increasingly unruly and agitated . After the stampede, community centers became makeshift facilities for missing persons as friends desperately sought for their loved ones. After the president declared a period of national mourning on Sunday, he visited the site of the stampede. He expressed condolences to the victims, most of whom were in their 20s. The disaster was the country’s deadliest since the 2014 ferry sinking that killed 304 people, mainly high school students. Difficult words: stampede (a sudden panic and movement of many people at the same time), agitated (upset or nervous), makeshift (temporary). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

153 people died at a Halloween festival in Seoul, South Korea. The incident happened in a popular nightlife area. The event was the first since the pandemic when people didn’t have to wear masks or follow safety rules . A crowd of people moved into a narrow street that made movement impossible. The situation got out of control at around 10 pm when some people became drunk and unruly . They continued to walk, although the place was already full. Some people fell to the ground and others crushed them. The incident became one of the biggest disasters since 2014 when 304 students died in a ferry accident. On Sunday, the country’s president visited the area, and he declared a time of national mourning . Difficult words: safety rule (behaviors which people follow to keep safe), unruly (wild and without control), mourn (to feel or show deep sadness when someone dies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Halloween festival is in Seoul, South Korea. People are happy. The event is the first with no coronavirus restrictions . The festival takes place in a popular area. Many clubs and bars are there. One narrow street becomes full of people. They cannot move. It is nighttime. People can’t see well. Some people become crazy. They don’t see how serious the situation is. People fall to the ground. Others step on them. 153 people die. Many of these people are around 20 years old. The disaster is one of the country’s biggest. On Sunday, South Korea’s president visits the place. A time of national mourning is happening in the country now. Difficult words: restriction (a rule which tells what people can or cannot do), disaster (a very serious accident in which people get hurt or die), national mourning (when the people of a country are very sad when someone gets hurt or dies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Paul Pelosi is the husband of House Speaker Nancy Pelosi; an intruder assaulted him in his own home in San Francisco, California, USA. The attacker was 42-year-old David DePape. He was active in online right-wing conspiracy groups, and he often posted conspiracy-related content on Facebook. DePape reportedly entered the house when he broke a rear window of the property, and he demanded to see Nancy, who was in Washington DC at the time. He viciously attacked Paul Pelosi with a hammer, which caused a skull fracture. Pelosi underwent a surgery for his injuries, and he’s currently recovering. The investigation is still ongoing; however, police have claimed that the attack was premeditated . They have charged DePape with attempted homicide . Difficult words: viciously (in an aggressive or angry way), premeditate (to plan something beforehand), homicide (a murder). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man attacked Paul Pelosi who is the husband of politician Nancy Pelosi. He attacked him in his home in San Francisco, California, USA. Police identified the attacker as 42-year-old David DePape. He broke the back window of the house to get inside. He asked where Nancy Pelosi was, but she wasn’t there because she was in Washington DC. DePape attacked her husband with a hammer, which caused a skull fracture . Pelosi underwent surgery, and he was recovering from it. DePape often posted conspiracy content on social media, and police say that he planned the attack carefully. They charged DePape with attempted homicide . Difficult words: skull fracture (a break in bones in the head), conspiracy (a secret plan by a group of people to do something illegal or dangerous), homicide (a murder). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nancy Pelosi is an American politician. She is the House Speaker . She lives with her husband in their home in San Francisco, California. A man breaks a back window in her house. He gets into the house. He wants to meet Nancy Pelosi. She is not inside. She is in Washington DC. The man attacks Nancy’s husband named Paul. He attacks Paul with a hammer. He breaks his head. Paul just get a surgery. The attacker is David DePape. He is 42 years old. Police say that he plans the attack carefully. He posts conspiracy ideas on social media. Police say he has attempted homicide . Difficult words: House Speaker (the leader of the House of Representatives; it is a group in the US government), conspiracy (a secret plan by a group of powerful people), attempted homicide (when a person tries to kill someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Health officials are getting worried about the so-called “triple-demic”; it is an onslaught of three major respiratory illnesses in the upcoming winter season. A surge in cases of respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, and an increase in COVID-19 both came earlier than the normal flu season this year. Infants under age 5 and adults over 65 are mostly impacted by RSV. Emergency rooms are already impacted by the surge, and according to experts, children may be getting sick because of social distancing or masks. Among older individuals, the virus causes pneumonia , and it’s very hard to distinguish from influenza or COVID-19. Meanwhile, data shows that the coronavirus is still spreading, and in the US, there are 260,000 new cases and over 2,500 deaths reported weekly. The US President Joe Biden urged more people to get the booster vaccine before the upcoming winter season. Difficult words: onslaught (a very large number), pneumonia (an infection of the lungs), distinguish (to be able to tell one thing from another). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Doctors worry about the coming winter and so-called “triple-demic”. They believe that cases of three big respiratory illnesses will increase again. This year, the season of respiratory illnesses started earlier than usual. Doctors say that one of the reasons could be the pandemic. Children spent several years without contact with each other, and their immunity is not very strong. Respiratory syncytial virus RSV affects mostly children under the age of five and adults over the age of 65. Its symptoms are very similar to flu or COVID-19. The coronavirus is also spreading around the world. In the US, 260,000 new people get tested every week and over 2,500 deaths happen from it. On Thursday, the US president asked people to get the booster vaccine before the winter starts. Difficult words: respiratory (breath), immunity (the ability of the body to fight a disease), booster vaccine (a medicine that protects you and makes the effect of a previous vaccine stronger). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Doctors worry about this year’s winter. Many people are sick from a respiratory virus called RSV. RSV is dangerous for small children. It is also dangerous for people over 65 years old. This virus has many symptoms similar to COVID-19 or flu. People get sick from it early this year. Children aren’t around each other during the coronavirus. Their immunity is not so strong. They become easily ill. Many children and older people are already ill. Many people are also sick from the coronavirus. In the US, 260,000 people get ill every week. More than 2,500 people die from the coronavirus every week. The US president asks people to get medicine to protect them. They must do it before the winter starts. Difficult words: respiratory (breathes), symptom (a sign that tells us that somebody is ill), immunity (how the body fights with a disease). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Safaricom has launched a 5G network as the first company to deploy the technology in East Africa. Safaricom uses equipment from Nokia and Huawei to power its network, and it offers subscriptions to get more people in the fixed data market. The company dominates about 65% of the mobile data market; however, it only has 30% of the fixed data market. Safaricom said it would focus on 5G Wi-Fi rather than mobile because few 5G- compatible devices are in Kenya due to the high cost. However, prices were going down quickly, and the company was improving access to 5G technology. The company has 35 active 5G sites in Nairobi and other major cities, and it plans to increase the number to 200 by March of next year. Difficult words: deploy (to bring into action), dominate (to be in control of), compatible (work with something else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Safaricom became the first company to start a 5G network in East Africa. The company has 35 5G sites in Nairobi and several other cities in Kenya, but it plans to have 200 sites in spring next year. With 65% control, Safaricom is the leader on the market with mobile data, but it wants to increase its control of fixed data . The problem is that out of 27 million smartphones in Kenya, only a few of them can use 5G. 5G phones have high prices, but the prices are actually going down fast. For this reason, Safaricom wants to focus on 5G wifi rather than mobile data. Safaricom is thinking about how to make 5G technology more accessible , and one idea is to offer fixed data subscriptions. Difficult words: fixed data (Internet data which requires a computer or terminal), accessible (when many people can have something), subscription (when people pay some money every month to get a service). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Safaricom is a company. It provides 5G technology. It is the first company to start this business in East Africa. Safaricom has 35 5G sites in Nairobi and other cities in Kenya. The company wants to have 200 sites in spring next year. It does a lot of business with mobile data . The company wants to do more business with fixed data . The change is not easy. Many smartphones in Africa can’t use the 5G network. New phones are very expensive. Luckily, the prices are going down quickly. Safaricom wants to make 5G available to more people. One idea is to offer subscriptions. Then people pay some money every month. They get fixed data. Difficult words: 5G (modern fast Internet), mobile data (Internet data in a person’s phone), fixed data (Internet data that needs a computer or terminal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Coca-Cola unveiled its FIFA World Cup campaign anthem. The song’s a multicultural rework of Queen’s iconic 1986 track ‘A Kind of Magic’, and it fuses a flavor of Arabic and Latin culture. The song features three female artists, Mexican singer Danna Paola, Egyptian neo-soul and rap star Felukah, and Saudi Arabian singer and songwriter Tamtam. People filmed the music video in Mexico City. In addition to this track, Coca-Cola is energizing their campaign with elements of digital films, packaging, and a Fan Zone, which bring together football fans worldwide. The World Cup starts on November 20 in Qatar, and it’ll last to December 18. 32 teams will compete across 64 matches in the 22 nd edition of this competition. Difficult words: iconic (very famous or popular), fuse (to unite), element (a basic but important part of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Coca-Cola introduced its campaign song for the 2022 FIFA World Cup. FIFA’s 22 nd world cup starts on November 20, and it ends on December 18. The event will happen in Qatar, and 32 football teams will compete in 64 matches. Three female artists from Mexico, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia cooperated on the song, which was filmed in Mexico. The song was a rework of a popular 1986 Queen song ‘A Kind of Magic’. Additionally, the Coca-Cola prepared digital films, special packaging, and a fan zone , which will bring together football fans from all the world. Difficult words: campaign (an organized action to achieve or promote something), rework (a new version of something, for example, a book, song, or film), fan zone (an area outside a sports stadium where people can watch a game on a large screen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Coca-Cola makes a song. It is for the 2022 FIFA World Cup. It is FIFA’s 22nd World Cup. Three female singers make the song. They are from Mexico, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia. They change a popular Queen song from 1986. It is named ‘A Kind of Magic’. The new song mixes Arabic and Latin music. The World Cup will happen in Qatar. It will start on November 20. It will end on December 18. 32 football teams will play. 64 matches will happen. Coca-Cola wants to bring together football fans from all the world. It also makes digital films. It makes new packaging for its products. It also plans a fan zone outside the matches. Difficult words: female (a woman), packaging (the container for a product), fan zone (a place where people can watch a game on a large screen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Global currents deposit marine debris from all over the world on Kenya’s beaches which is a big problem for turtles. A report found that 23% of juvenile and 54% of post- hatchling turtles ingested plastic, suggesting that young turtles are more likely to die than the adults by eating plastic. Hassan Mohammed from the World Wildlife Fund said that turtles sometimes confuse plastics for food, thinking that they are jellyfish. Moreover, when there are a lot of plastics around hatching sites, turtles are unable to lay eggs and when baby turtles hatch, they cannot reach the ocean. Out of every 1,000 turtles hatched, only one grows into adulthood, according to the WWF. Difficult words: current (the moving of water), deposit (move to a place), debris (waste), juvenile (young), hatchling (a young animal which just came out from its egg). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Water deposits plastic waste from all over the world on Kenya’s beaches. That is a big problem for turtles as many of them eat the plastic because they think that it is jellyfish, and then they die. A new report found that young turtles die more often than adults because of plastic. Moreover, when there are a lot of plastics on beaches, turtles cannot lay eggs. When the baby turtles hatch on beaches with plastics, they cannot get to the ocean. Out of every 1,000 turtles hatched, only one grows into adulthood, according to the WWF . Difficult words: deposit (move to a place), hatch (come out of its egg), WWF (an organisation which tries to protect animals and nature). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Kenya’s beaches, there is a lot of plastic waste . This is a big problem for turtles. They eat the plastic. The plastic kills them. They eat it because they think that it is jellyfish . People find out that young turtles eat plastic more often than adults . They die, also. When there is plastic on beaches, turtles cannot lay eggs. Plastics also blocks the way to the ocean. This is a problem for young turtles. They cannot get into the water. Difficult words: waste (things which you throw away), jellyfish (a sea animal), adult Turtles and Plastic (bigger and older). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

From its all-time high in March this year, aluminium has experienced a spectacular fall of over 40%. A combination of factors contributed to the fall. First, global interest rates dramatically rose even as the US tried to fight inflation. Second, metals have become more expensive with still relatively high yields . However, high rates slowed business and demand for building materials. In Europe, energy concerns related to embargoes on Russian supplies may continue in the coming months. At the same time, China will continue on its zero COVID-19 policy, so the demand may not increase from that part of the world. More recent data shows a significant increase of aluminium value at the London metals exchange, and some experts are speculating about the potential dumping of Russian aluminium. Difficult words: yield (profit), embargo (an official ban on trade with a particular country), speculate (to form opinions about something without having the necessary information). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In March 2022, prices of aluminium reached record levels, but since that time, they decreased over 40%. A few reasons explain why it happened. The first reason is rising interest rates in the world, which influence the prices of materials. Metals became very expensive, which had an impact on the building business. The need for metals went down, but some companies made profits . The second reason is the war in Ukraine and Russia’s business with the EU. People cannot easily predict how the situation will develop, and many things influence the business, for example, China’s need for metals. Currently, experts at a London trading area see that more aluminium is for sale. Some people believe that companies are getting rid of Russian aluminium. Difficult words: interest rate (the money a bank charges someone who borrows money), profit (money which a business earns), get rid (to throw away or destroy something that you don’t want anymore). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Aluminium is a light silver metal. In March 2022, its price very high. Now, the price of aluminium is 40% lower. Many reasons influence the situation. First, banks in all the world raise their interest rates . Metals become more expensive. The cost hurts building companies. Companies buy less aluminium. Second, the war in Ukraine has hurt business in Russia. Prices are growing. People cannot easily say what will happen. Experts at the London exchange see people can buy more aluminum now. They think that some companies sell aluminium from Russia. They want to sell it quickly. Difficult words: influence (to have an impact on something), interest rate (how much money a bank wants when someone borrows money from it), exchange (a place where companies make business with a specific material or product). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Swedish marine archaeologists found a shipwreck of the ship Applet; they believed it was the long-lost sister ship of the warship Vasa. Vasa was 69 meters long, and it sank on its maiden voyage in Stockholm in 1628 after sailing just over 900 meters. Vasa is known as the world’s best preserved 17 th century ship. The same shipbuilder constructed Applet, and it launched in 1629. When divers discovered the shipwreck, they found it to was similar to Vasa. Both the construction and the powerful dimensions sparked the hope of finding one of its sister ships. Parts of the ship’s side had sunk to the bottom of the sea; however, the hull was preserved to a lower gun deck. Archaeologists said that Applet will stay on the seabed where the water protects it. Difficult words: maiden voyage (the first journey), hull (the main body of a ship or other vessel), gun deck (a part of a ship that has cannons from end to end). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Swedish archaeologist s found a shipwreck of a 17 th century ship. The name of the ship was Applet, and it was a sister ship of the warship Vasa. Workers built Vasa in 1628, and unfortunately, it sank on its first journey near Stockholm after it sailed only 900 meters. The ship is 69 meters long and it is the world’s best preserved ship from the 17 th century. The same shipbuilder of Vasa also built Applet in 1629. When divers found the shipwreck, they hoped that it was Applet. A part of the ship sank to the bottom, but the main body remained. Archaeologists decided to leave Applet in the sea because removal was too difficult. Difficult words: archaeologist (a person who studies very old things), shipwreck (a ship which sinks at sea), preserved (when something looks the same as it looked a long time ago). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Swedish divers find a shipwreck . They think that it is Applet. Applet is a ship from 1629. It is a warship. A part of the ship sinks to the bottom of the sea. The main part of the ship doesn’t break. The ship is very big. It looks very similar to Vasa. Vasa is another warship from 1628. Vasa is the best preserved ship in the world. It is 69 meters long. It sinks on its first journey. The ship sails only 900 meters. Archaeologists will leave Applet in the sea. The work to take it out is difficult. It could break. Difficult words: shipwreck (a ship which sinks at sea), preserved (when something old looks as new), archaeologist (a person who studies old things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Mississippi River is America’s largest river, and it’s drying up; the bottom of the river is now massive sand dunes . The water levels are dropping to record lows near Memphis, Tennessee, which are more than three meters below expected. The US mega drought is expanding to 59% of the states. The situation’s getting worse mostly in the Great Plains in the Midwest, as the drought covers almost all of the Mississippi’s tributaries . The low levels of many rivers are devastating the agricultural industry and the whole transportation network in the Midwest. Low water levels carry much less cargo, and farmers have few options to send soybeans, corn and grains to international markets. They have to wait for the water to get deeper. Clearly, people will have to learn to adapt to the changing climate and the continuing drop in water levels. Difficult words: dune (a hill of sand), tributary (a river that flows into a larger river or lake), devastating (great damage or harm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Big heatwaves in the US are bringing drought , which has a bad impact on rivers. The water levels of many US rivers are dropping. In some areas, people cannot travel by boats because the water is not deep enough. The Mississippi River is the largest river in the US, and some parts of it are very different now than a decade ago. Some of it is sand dunes , and people can walk on the bottom of the river. The drought affected almost all of the Mississippi’s tributaries , and farmers cannot easily sell their crops. Farmers use big boats to move their crops from fields to international markets. The rivers are not deep enough for these big boats; farmers must use smaller boats which carry less crops. Difficult words: drought (a period of time when it rains very little), dune (a hill of sand), tributary (a river which adds water into a larger river). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Mississippi River is big. It is the US’s largest river. It is drying up . It doesn’t have enough. Many rivers flow into the Mississippi. Most of these rivers are in the Midwest. This area has many problems from drought . The weather has very little rain here. In some places, people can walk on the bottom of rivers. Big boats can’t go on these rivers. The water is too low. Farmers use big boats to move food. The rivers are not deep enough for the boats. Farmers must use smaller boats. Farmers have problems. They can’t sell all their food. The weather is changing. It hurts the farmers. They must learn to live with the changes. Difficult words: dry up (to get dry), flow (to move water), drought (a time when it doesn’t rain in an area for a long time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2021, 15-year-old Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva tested positive for a banned heart medication at the Russian National Championship. However, Valieva was allowed to compete in the single event. Some months later, she also competed at the Beijing Winter Olympics, where she won the gold medal for her team. In her defense, Valieva claimed that the positive test result was allegedly because of a mix-up with her grandfather’s heart medication. Russia’s anti-doping agency said that it wouldn’t release investigation results to protect the interests of the figure skater. The agency said that it strictly follows principles on international and Russian anti-doping standards, but it also considered the case’s facts and circumstances of the case. Difficult words: mix-up (a confusion of one thing with another), anti-doping agency (an organization that fights against the use of drugs in sports), principle (a moral rule or standard). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last year, Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva competed at the Russian National Championship. After the competition, Valieva tested positive for an illegal heart drug . Valieva said that she made a mistake, and she took her grandfather’s heart pills. A few months later, officials allowed her to compete at the Beijing Winter Olympics, where she won the gold medal. Russia’s anti-doping agency started to investigate the doping scandal , and this week, it knew the results. The agency won’t say the results because it wants to protect the skater. Only the agency knows the results. It said it follows all international and Russian anti-doping rules. Difficult words: drug (a medicine), anti-doping agency (an organization which checks if athletes take illegal medicines), scandal (an event which makes many people angry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kamila Valieva is a Russian figure skater . She is 16 years old. Last year, she skates at the Russian National Championship. Valieva gets a drug test after the event. She has a positive test for a heart medicine. This medicine is illegal in sports. She says that she makes a mistake. She takes her grandfather’s heart pills. A few months later, officials allow Valieva to skate at the Winter Olympics in Beijing, China. Valieva wins the gold medal. Her win is a big scandal . This week, a Russian drug organization says that it knows the results of Valieva’s case. The organization won’t say the result. It says that it wants to protect the skater. Difficult words: figure skater (an athlete who moves quickly and jumps on ice), illegal (against the law or rules), scandal (something which makes many people angry). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Polio is a highly infectious disease caused by one of three polio virus types. The virus reproduces in the human gastrointestinal tract . Infected people spread the virus in their feces; therefore, the virus spreads easily in areas without good sanitation and hygiene. For years, humans have been close to eradicating polio; however, it’s very difficult because fewer than one in 100 infected people show signs of illness or are aware or the infection. They unintentionally give the virus to others. A combination of old and new challenges is setting back the global fight. They include the war in Ukraine, floods in Pakistan, vaccine worries, and the COVID-19 pandemic. New polio outbreaks happened in Africa, and the disease paralyzed a man in the US. The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation has pledged 1.2 billion dollars to eradicate the disease, and humans hope that we will stop all polio by the end of 2023. Difficult words: gastrointestinal tract (the area of the body where you digest food), sanitation (service to keep clean and healthy), eradicate (to get rid of something completely). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Polio is a highly infectious and dangerous disease. The virus lives in the digestive system . The virus spreads easily in places with bad sanitation . For more than 35 years, people almost completely destroyed the virus, but it was difficult. Only some people show any signs of being ill, and many infected people don’t know that they are ill. People almost destroyed the virus, but events like the COVID-19 pandemic and floods in Pakistan made the situation worse again. Bill and Melinda Gates donated 1.2 billion dollars to stop polio, and some experts said that it should stop by the end of 2023. Difficult words: digestive system (the body parts which work with food in the body), sanitation (keep places clean and healthy), donate (to give money for something good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Polio is a disease. It is very dangerous for small children. It can leave a person paralyzed. You cannot move. A virus causes the disease. The virus lives in the digestive system . It moves in dirty places. Many people don’t know that they are ill. Only some people have symptoms . The symptoms are often a sore throat and a fever. People don’t know that they are ill. The disease moves more easily. Humans try to end polio. They try for more than 35 years. Some events happen. They are events like COVID-19 and floods in Pakistan. They make the fight more difficult. Bill and Melinda Gates donate 1.2 billion dollars. They want to stop polio. Experts hope that this change will happen next year. Difficult words: digestive system (the body parts which change food in the body), symptoms (a change in the body which shows that someone is ill), donate (to give money for something good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last week, a woman in Massachusetts, US, used a swarm of bees to attack police. The incident unfolded when Rorie Woods, a 55-year-old professional beekeeper, drove up to a house in Longmeadow. Police were in the process of enforcing an eviction notice on a residence, which belonged to a man who had been litigating against his removal for years. He had support of anti-eviction activists, including Woods. The beekeeper intentionally agitated the bees, and she opened one of the beehives. A sheriff’s deputy tried to stop her, but the angry bees started circling the area. The bees stung several officers and bystanders, who went to the hospital. The Hampden County sheriff told Woods that some people there were allergic to bees, and the woman responded that it was good. She now has several charges of assault and battery by means of a dangerous weapon. Difficult words: eviction (a situation when police force someone from a property), litigate (to take legal action), battery (hurt someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man lived in a house in Massachusetts, US, for many years. Authorities asked the man to move, but he didn’t do it. He took legal action against the local authorities, and many people supported him. One of the people was 55-year-old Rorie Woods. Last week, she drove to the man’s house as police were there to get the man out. Woods was a beekeeper , and she had several beehives stacked on her car. She wanted the officers to leave. She opened one of the beehives and disturbed the bees. The bees got out, and they stung several people. Police arrested the woman. The county’s sheriff said that he had never seen anyone attack others with bees before. Difficult words: beekeeper (a person who keeps bees for their honey), beehive (a box in which people keep bees), disturb (to make nervous or upset). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man lives in a house in Massachusetts, US. Authorities say that the man must leave. The man doesn’t want to do it. Many people support him. Rorie Woods is one of them. She is 55 years old. She is a beekeeper. She keeps bees for their honey. Last week, Woods drives to the man’s house. The police are there. They ask the man to leave the house. Woods has beehives on her car. She opens one beehive. The bees get out. They sting several people. Police arrest the woman. Police say that they never see someone attack people with bees before. Difficult words: support (to help), beehive (a box in which people keep bees), sting (to hurt someone from an insect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tarantulas are a popular delicacy in Cambodia; so much so that the high demand is causing a decline in the species .
